newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse plans major capacity increase - CEO.
newsitem.headline: German bourse plans major capacity increase - CEO.

text.p: German bourse operators Deutsche Boerse AG said on Wednesday the bourse plans to significantly increase system capacity this week, following a series of interruptions to share trade amid massive volumes.
Bourse CEO Werner Seifert told Reuters: "By Saturday at the latest, capacities will be 3.5 million (transactions) plus 'X' percent. 'X' certainly means more than five percent."

Seifert also said that the technical interruptions would not affect the introduction of Xetra, the new 150 million mark ($82.4 million) electronic trading system which is scheduled to replace IBIS later this year.
Massive volumes amid surging prices on Germany's financial markets on Wednesday overloaded trading systems and forced a temporary shutdown of both floor and electronic trading.
There were 3.5 million transactions on the bourse on Wednesday, twice as many as the previous high.
Seifert said the shutdowns had not cost market players in volume terms, because trading times had been extended. "Also no investor has been badly affected," Seifert said.

Seifert said the introduction of the new Xetra system would not be affected. Xetra will deal, at first, only with wholesale orders, but expand by the end of 1998 to become a full competitor to traditional floor trading.
The system will be order-driven, offering automatic price matches and eliminating the need for intermediaries.
